correctness.rationale: All possible coordinates are classified via four torus-fixed chart types. The semigroup cones are proved exactly through resource-allocation decompositions; every candidate facet has full supporting rank and is primitive; the coordinate facet normals form an integral basis so divisor-class groups are torsion-free of predicted rank. Canonical Cartier tests force the unique all-ones character, evaluating the exceptional facets to a-2 or b-2. Connected bipartite graph normality uses Ohsugi--Hibi Corollary 2.3. A freshly generated packaged checker tests 292 charts for 3<=a,b<=6 and reproduces output. Finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The contribution is the complete local class-group trichotomy, the new rank-two cross charts, and the sharp projective Q-Gorenstein condition, not known adjacency or general toric textbook machinery. Ohsugi--Hibi (2008) supplies graph-edge adjacency but not the local divisor-class/canonical classification; Bigdeli--Herzog--Lu concerns one deletion and deformations. More general Ehrhart Gorenstein criteria concern a different ring. Source-specific implication comparisons and unresolved risks are recorded.

value.rationale: The study determines an intrinsic birational invariant (the Zariski local Weil divisor class group) at all torus-fixed points of a geometrically natural infinite family, exhibits a genuinely new two-deletion cross-chart rank jump from one to two, and yields a sharp canonical Cartier phase boundary. The two-cross-facet interaction is not visible in global adjacency totals or one-deletion strata. This exact structural classification informs local factoriality and possible birational models; no stronger application or universal priority is claimed.
